claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has a porous microstructure.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 has limited mechanical integrity under the stated service conditions.
A minute silica-based additive will form an in situ transient liquid phase during ZrB2 sintering.
The silica-based additive will enable ZrB2 densification at approximately 2200 °C.
The transient liquid phase will enhance mass transport in the ZrB2 compact.
The transient liquid phase will enhance particle rearrangement in the ZrB2 compact.
Enhanced mass transport and particle rearrangement will produce a denser microstructure with fewer residual pores.
The silica-based additive melts at a temperature low enough to generate the proposed transient liquid phase during the specified sintering treatment.
Localized mass transfer and liquid-phase sintering will accelerate densification and minimize residual-pore formation.
After densification, the additive will react with the matrix or evaporate.
Removal or reaction of the additive will leave a single-phase ZrB2 ceramic.
Reduced porosity will improve resistance to hole formation during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Reduced porosity will improve structural integrity during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Additive-modified ZrB2 sintered at approximately 2200 °C will have lower residual porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Additive-modified ZrB2 will form fewer holes than conventionally sintered ZrB2 during extended plating-bath exposure.
Additive-modified ZrB2 will retain greater mechanical integrity than conventionally sintered ZrB2 after extended plating-bath exposure.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator describes the resulting microstructure as pore-free, whereas the predicted outcome only claims significantly reduced residual porosity.

The mechanism states that reaction or evaporation ensures a single-phase final ceramic, while the uncertainty field explicitly states that complete reaction or volatilization and the absence of secondary phases are uncertain.
